title: 12 space-saving ideas for a 1BHK flat in Mumbai
desc: Practical space-saving ideas for small Mumbai flats: storage beds, wall units, folding tables and layout tricks that make a 1BHK feel bigger.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Most 1BHK flats in Mumbai, Thane and Navi Mumbai have between 350 and 550 sq ft of carpet area. That is not much room for a family, so every wall and every corner has to work. The good news is that a few smart choices make a small flat feel open and calm instead of cramped.
Here are the ideas we use most often when we plan small homes.
Make the bed do double duty
**Hydraulic storage bed:** the whole mattress lifts up and the base becomes a deep box for quilts, suitcases and seasonal clothes. It holds far more than drawers. See our [beds](/furniture/beds/).
**Bed with side drawers:** better if you cannot lift the mattress easily, or if there is a window beside the bed.
**Headboard with shelves:** a slim 6–8 inch shelf behind the pillows replaces two side tables.

Mumbai flats usually have 9 to 10 feet of ceiling height. A wardrobe that stops at 7 feet wastes the top 2–3 feet. Ask for a **loft** above the wardrobe and above the bedroom and kitchen doors. Lofts are perfect for things you use a few times a year.
Keep everyday items between knee and eye level. Lofts are for storage, not for things you need every morning.
Choose sliding instead of hinged shutters

A hinged wardrobe door needs about 2 feet of clear space in front of it. In a narrow bedroom, a **sliding wardrobe** saves that space and lets you place the bed closer. Our [wardrobe guide](/blog/sliding-vs-hinged-wardrobe/) explains when each type works best.
Pick furniture that folds or nests
A **wall-mounted folding dining table** that opens for meals and folds flat afterwards.
**Nesting tables** — two or three small tables that slide under each other.
A **sofa cum bed** for guests, if you do not have a second bedroom.
**Stackable chairs** that live in a corner when not needed.
Choose a sofa with **raised legs**; seeing the floor under furniture makes a room look bigger.
Use light colours on large surfaces — walls, wardrobe shutters and curtains — and add colour in cushions and art.
A wall-mounted [TV unit](/furniture/tv-units/) with a floating base cabinet keeps the floor clear and is easier to clean.
One large mirror opposite a window doubles the daylight.
A shoe cabinet with a seat on top, a few hooks for bags and a small key tray stop clutter from spreading into the living room. Even a 2-foot wide unit near the door makes a big difference.

In a small kitchen, tall units and a **pull-out pantry** beside the fridge store more than base cabinets alone. A corner carousel or magic corner uses the dead space in an L-shaped counter. Read more in our [modular kitchen cost guide](/guides/modular-kitchen-cost-mumbai/).
Get the sizes right before you buy

The most common mistake we see is furniture bought online that does not fit — a sofa that blocks the balcony door, or a bed that leaves no room to open the wardrobe. Measure the room, mark the furniture outline on the floor with tape, and walk around it for a day. Or ask us to measure and make the piece to the exact size; that is what [furniture to measure](/services/furniture-to-measure/) is for.
Hydraulic storage bed, sliding wardrobe with loft
Raised-leg sofa, wall-mounted TV unit, mirror
Folding wall table or 4-seater with bench
Shoe cabinet with seat and hooks
Tall pantry unit, corner solution, lofts
A well planned 1BHK can store as much as a badly planned 2BHK. If you want help, send us a photo and the room sizes on WhatsApp and we will suggest a layout.

title: Monsoon care for wooden furniture in Mumbai
desc: How Mumbai monsoon humidity affects wood and plywood furniture, and simple steps to stop swelling, fungus, sticking doors and bad smells.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: From June to September, humidity in Mumbai often stays above 80 percent. Wood and plywood absorb moisture from the air, and that is when doors start sticking, drawers jam and a musty smell appears inside wardrobes. A little care before and during the rains prevents most of these problems.
Why furniture suffers in the monsoon

Wood is a natural material. It takes in moisture when the air is wet and releases it when the air is dry. This makes solid wood **swell slightly** across the grain, which is why a shutter that closed easily in March can rub in July. Plywood and MDF are more stable, but their **edges** absorb water quickly if the edge banding is damaged.
**Check the edges.** Look at the bottom edges of wardrobe and kitchen shutters. If the edge banding is peeling, get it re-pasted now.
**Polish solid wood.** A fresh coat of melamine or PU polish seals the surface. Do it in April or May, when the wood is dry.
**Move furniture slightly away from walls.** Keep a gap of about 1–2 inches, especially on outer walls that get wet. Damp walls are the biggest cause of fungus behind wardrobes.
**Fix leaks first.** If a wall gets damp every year, no polish will save the wardrobe against it. Get the waterproofing done.
**Open wardrobes for a few minutes every day** so air can move inside.
Put **silica gel packets or moisture absorbers** in wardrobes and drawers and replace them when full.
Keep **naphthalene balls or neem leaves** away from direct contact with clothes, but inside the wardrobe to discourage insects.
Wipe up water immediately — from wet umbrellas, plants and mopping — before it reaches the furniture legs.
Run a **fan or dehumidifier** in closed rooms for a while each day.
Never wipe wooden furniture with a dripping wet cloth in the monsoon. Use a damp, well-wrung cloth, then a dry one.

Do not plane or cut a sticking door during the rains. Once the dry season comes, the wood shrinks back and the door will have a gap. Instead, ask a carpenter to **adjust the hinges** slightly. Most modern hinges have adjustment screws for exactly this.
If you see white spots or fungus

Wipe the area with a cloth dipped in a mild solution of white vinegar and water, then dry it fully and keep the area ventilated. If the fungus keeps coming back, the cause is usually a damp wall behind the furniture.
Choose the right material next time
If you are building new furniture, ask for:
BWR plywood with a laminate on the back side too
Edge banding on all four edges, applied by machine
Our [plywood, MDF and solid wood guide](/guides/plywood-mdf-solid-wood-furniture/) explains the grades in more detail.
With these habits, good furniture easily lasts many Mumbai monsoons.

title: Teak vs sheesham vs engineered wood: which is right for you?
desc: A plain comparison of teak, sheesham and engineered wood for furniture in Mumbai — strength, look, price and which to choose for each room.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: When you order furniture, one of the first questions is what it should be made of. In Mumbai, most furniture is made from teak, sheesham (Indian rosewood) or engineered wood such as plywood and MDF. Each has a place. Here is how they compare, in plain language.
Teak is the traditional favourite for doors, beds and dining tables. It contains natural oils that help it resist moisture and termites, which is why it does well in a humid city.
**Strengths:** very durable, stable, ages beautifully, takes polish well.
**Weaknesses:** the most expensive option; good-quality, well-seasoned teak is not always easy to find.
**Best for:** main doors, dining tables, beds and heirloom pieces.
Sheesham is a dense hardwood with a rich brown colour and strong grain. It is popular for sofas frames, beds, chairs and tables.
**Strengths:** strong and heavy, attractive grain, usually costs less than teak.
**Weaknesses:** must be **properly seasoned**, otherwise it can crack or warp. Heavier to move.
**Best for:** beds, dining sets, coffee tables and chairs.
Most wardrobes, kitchens, TV units and office furniture today are made from engineered boards with a laminate, veneer or acrylic finish.
**Plywood** is made of thin wood layers glued together. It holds screws well and is strong. Use BWR grade for most furniture and BWP grade for wet areas.
**MDF** is smooth and good for painted or routed designs, but weaker against water and heavy loads.
**Particle board** is the cheapest and is mostly used in ready-made flat-pack furniture.
For built-in wardrobes and kitchens, good plywood with a quality laminate is usually the best value. Save solid wood for pieces you will see and touch every day.
How to check what you are paying for
Ask for the **wood type and grade in writing** in your quotation.
For plywood, ask for the **brand and grade** (for example BWR or BWP) and check the stamp on the sheet when it arrives.
For solid wood, ask if it is **seasoned** and how.
Ask about **termite treatment** for any solid wood.

Our workshop makes furniture in all three materials, so we can suggest what suits your budget. See our [furniture made to measure](/services/furniture-to-measure/) or read the detailed [plywood, MDF and solid wood guide](/guides/plywood-mdf-solid-wood-furniture/).

title: Laminate, veneer, acrylic or PU: choosing a furniture finish
desc: Laminate, veneer, acrylic and PU finishes compared for wardrobes, kitchens and TV units: looks, durability, cleaning and budget.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: The finish is what you see and touch every day, so it decides how your wardrobe, kitchen or TV unit looks — and how well it survives daily use. Here are the four finishes we are asked about most.
Laminate is a thin, tough sheet pressed onto plywood. It comes in hundreds of colours and textures — plain matt, wood grain, stone, fabric and high gloss.
Scratch- and stain-resistant, easy to clean.
Good value; the most popular choice for wardrobes and kitchens.
Thicker laminates (around 1 mm) last much longer than thin decorative sheets.
Veneer is a real wood slice, polished after it is pasted on the board. Each sheet is unique, so it gives the warm look of solid wood at a lower cost.
Needs polishing and is more delicate than laminate; avoid it near water.
Best for living rooms, bedrooms, wall panelling and bedroom furniture.
Acrylic sheets give a mirror-like high-gloss finish in bright or pastel colours.
Very modern look, popular for kitchens.
Fingerprints and fine scratches show more easily; wipe with a soft microfibre cloth.
PU is a sprayed paint finish in matt, satin or gloss. It gives a smooth, seamless look with no visible edges.
Any colour you want, very elegant.
Most expensive and needs a skilled painter and a dust-free spray area.
Repairs are harder to match than laminate.
Ask for the laminate catalogue name and number in your quotation, so you get exactly the shade you saw in the showroom.
Edges matter as much as the surface

Whatever finish you choose, ask how the **edges** will be done. Machine-pressed edge banding that matches the shutter colour looks neat and keeps moisture out. Poor edging is the first thing to peel in Mumbai's humidity — see our [monsoon care tips](/blog/monsoon-care-wooden-furniture-mumbai/).

Roughly, from lowest to highest cost: **laminate, veneer, acrylic, PU**. For a full wardrobe or kitchen, the difference between laminate and PU can be a large share of the total. Many families mix finishes — acrylic on the upper kitchen shutters and laminate below, for example — to get the look at a lower cost. Our [modular kitchen cost guide](/guides/modular-kitchen-cost-mumbai/) has per square foot figures.

title: How to choose the right sofa: size, foam, fabric and frame
desc: A practical sofa buying guide for Indian homes: measuring the room, seat depth, foam density, fabrics that suit Mumbai weather and frame quality.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: A sofa is one of the most used pieces of furniture in any home, and one of the hardest to judge in a shop. It can look perfect and still feel uncomfortable after a month. Here is what to check before you buy or order one.
Measure the wall where the sofa will go and the walking space in front of it. Leave at least **2.5 to 3 feet** between the sofa and the TV unit or coffee table for easy movement.
Measure the **lift, staircase and main door**. Many large sofas cannot reach upper floors in older buildings. Sofas made to order can be built in parts that join inside the home.
Decide the shape: a **3-seater** suits most living rooms; an **L-shape** gives more seating for the same wall length but needs a corner.
Shorter people prefer a shallower seat; if you like to sit cross-legged or lie down, go deeper. Always sit on a sample for a few minutes, not a few seconds.
The foam decides whether the sofa stays comfortable for years or sinks in months.
Ask for **high-density foam** in the seat. Seat foam around 32–40 kg/m³ density is common for good sofas.
**Fibre or feather-filled back cushions** feel softer and can be fluffed.
Removable cushion covers with zips make cleaning much easier.
**Cotton blends and linen look** fabrics breathe well in humid weather.
**Velvet** looks rich but attracts dust; choose a performance velvet that is easier to clean.
**Leatherette** is easy to wipe but can feel hot and sticky in summer and may peel after a few years.
With children or pets, choose a **darker or textured** fabric and ask for stain-resistant treatment.
Ask for a fabric sample to take home. Colours look different under home lights than in a showroom.

Look under the cushions and at the base. A good sofa has a **solid wood or strong plywood frame**, firm joints and a webbing or spring base. Avoid frames that creak or wobble when you sit at the edge.

Ready-made sofas are quick, but sizes are fixed. A sofa made to order fits your wall exactly, lets you choose the seat depth and fabric, and can be built in parts for difficult staircases. See our [sofa designs](/furniture/sofas/) for estimated prices, or [ask for a quote](/get-quote/).

title: Bed sizes in India: single, queen and king explained
desc: Standard bed and mattress sizes in India, how much room each needs, and how to choose between queen and king beds for Mumbai bedrooms.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Choosing the wrong bed size is one of the most common mistakes in small bedrooms. A king bed that leaves no space to open the wardrobe is not a luxury — it is a daily irritation. Here is a simple guide to bed sizes used in India.

The bed frame is usually **3 to 6 inches larger** than the mattress on each side, more if it has a padded headboard or side tables built in. Always confirm the mattress size **before** the bed is made.
How much space does a bed need?
Leave about **2 feet** of walking space on each side you use to get in and out.
Leave about **2.5 to 3 feet** in front of a wardrobe so the doors can open — less if the wardrobe is sliding.
At the foot of the bed, keep at least **2 feet** to walk past.
A simple test: mark the bed size on the floor with masking tape and live with it for a day before deciding.
**Queen** suits most master bedrooms in Mumbai flats and leaves room for side tables and a wardrobe.
**King** is comfortable for two adults and a small child, but needs a room of roughly 11 × 12 feet or more to feel comfortable.
In small second bedrooms, a **double** or a **single with a trundle** (a pull-out second bed) works well.
**Hydraulic storage:** the mattress base lifts up to reveal the full box below. Holds the most.
**Side drawers:** easier to use daily; need space beside the bed to pull out.
**No storage, raised legs:** lighter look and easier to clean under; good with a robot vacuum.

A bed height of around **18 to 20 inches** to the top of the mattress is comfortable for most adults, and easier for elders to get in and out of. A padded or panelled headboard makes reading in bed much more comfortable.
If your room has an odd shape, a window on one side or a pillar, a bed made to measure solves it. See our [beds](/furniture/beds/) for designs and estimated prices.

title: Sliding vs hinged wardrobe: which is better for your bedroom?
desc: Sliding or hinged wardrobe? Compare space needed, cost, storage, upkeep and looks to pick the right wardrobe for your Mumbai bedroom.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: A wardrobe is usually the largest piece of furniture in a bedroom, and the door type changes how the whole room works. Here is an honest comparison of sliding and hinged wardrobes.
Hinged (openable) shutters swing out like a normal door.
**Pros:** you can open the whole wardrobe at once; usually costs less; hinges are cheap and easy to replace; works with any shutter finish.
**Cons:** each door needs about **2 feet of clear space** in front of it; not ideal if the bed is close to the wardrobe.
Sliding shutters move on a top or bottom track, one panel in front of another.
**Pros:** no swing space needed, so the bed or dressing table can be closer; large panels look sleek; good for mirrors and glass.
**Cons:** you can only open part of the wardrobe at a time; good sliding systems cost more; tracks must be kept clean.
If the gap between your bed and wardrobe is less than about 2.5 feet, sliding is usually the better choice.
What makes a sliding wardrobe last
A **good-quality track and roller system** with soft-close.
Shutters that are **straight and not too heavy** — very tall panels can warp in humidity unless made with good board and balanced on both sides.
A proper **top channel** fixed to a strong loft or ceiling base.
The door type matters less than the inside layout. A good wardrobe has:
a **long hanging** section for dresses and kurtas,
a **double hanging** section (two rods) for shirts and trousers,
and a **loft** for bags and bedding.

Wardrobes are usually priced per square foot of front area. See our [wardrobe cost per sq ft guide](/guides/wardrobe-cost-per-sq-ft-mumbai/) for current ranges, and our [wardrobe designs](/furniture/wardrobes/) for ideas.

title: L-shape, parallel or straight: kitchen layouts for Mumbai flats
desc: The common modular kitchen layouts — straight, L-shape, parallel and U-shape — explained for Mumbai flats, with tips on the work triangle and storage.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Kitchens in Mumbai flats are usually compact, and the layout is mostly decided by where the window, door, gas line and plumbing are. Still, choosing the right layout for your space makes cooking easier and adds a lot of storage.

The three places you move between most are the **sink, the hob (gas stove) and the fridge**. Keep them close but not cramped — roughly 4 to 7 feet between each — and avoid putting the fridge where its door blocks the cooking area.
Best for **small 1BHK kitchens** and open kitchens facing the living room.
Add **tall units** and lofts to make up for limited counter space.
Counters on two walls meeting at a corner — the most common layout in Mumbai.
Separates cooking and washing areas well.
Use a **corner solution** (carousel, magic corner or blind corner pull-out) so the corner cabinet is not wasted.
Very efficient for narrow kitchens that are open at both ends.
Keep at least **3.5 to 4 feet** between the two counters so two people can work.
Usually the hob is on one side and the sink on the other.
The most storage and counter space; needs a wider kitchen.
Two corners to manage — plan corner fittings carefully.
Keep the **hob away from the window** if strong wind blows the flame.
Plan a **chimney** above the hob and an exhaust point.
A **tall pull-out pantry** holds a surprising amount of masala, grains and oil.
Put a **plug point** near the counter for the mixer, and another for the microwave or OTG.
A good kitchen is planned around how you cook. Tell your designer whether you make rotis daily, use a pressure cooker often, or store large quantities of grain.
For price per square foot by finish, read our [modular kitchen cost guide](/guides/modular-kitchen-cost-mumbai/), or see our [modular kitchen service](/services/modular-kitchens/).

title: Kitchen and wardrobe hardware: hinges, channels and fittings explained
desc: A simple guide to furniture hardware — hinges, drawer channels, tandem boxes, lift-ups and handles — and why good hardware matters more than looks.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: You can have the best plywood and the most beautiful finish, but if the hinges sag or the drawers jam, the furniture feels cheap. Hardware is a small part of the cost and a big part of daily comfort. Here is what you should know.
**Normal (clip-on) hinges** are the standard for cabinet shutters. They can be adjusted up, down and sideways with a screwdriver.
**Soft-close hinges** have a built-in damper so the door closes slowly and quietly. Worth it in kitchens and bedrooms.
**Hinge type depends on overlay:** full overlay (shutter covers the side panel), half overlay (two shutters share a panel) and inset. Your carpenter should choose the right one.
Complete drawer system with metal sides
Check the **load rating** — kitchen drawers holding utensils and pans need stronger channels than a wardrobe drawer.
**Cutlery and plate organisers** keep drawers tidy.
**Bottle pull-outs** next to the hob for oil and masala.
**Corner units** (carousel, magic corner) for L-shaped kitchens.
**Lift-up mechanisms** for upper cabinets, so you do not hit your head on open shutters.
**Wardrobe lift (pull-down rod)** for tall wardrobes, so you can reach clothes hung high.
**Trouser and tie racks, jewellery trays** and a **locker**.
**Sliding systems** with soft-close for sliding wardrobes.

Handles are both style and function. **Profile handles** (an aluminium strip along the edge) and **gola** (handle-less channel) systems give a clean modern look. Make sure older family members can grip them easily.
Ask for the hardware brand and type to be written in your quotation. "Soft-close channels" can mean very different quality levels.

For things you open many times a day — kitchen drawers, the main wardrobe, the TV unit — yes. For a loft you open twice a year, standard hardware is fine. A good split saves money without hurting daily use.
Want a kitchen with the right fittings? See our [modular kitchens](/services/modular-kitchens/).

title: TV unit design ideas for modern living rooms
desc: TV unit ideas for Indian living rooms: wall-mounted units, panelling, storage, the right TV height and viewing distance, and hiding wires.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: The TV wall is the focus of most living rooms. A well designed TV unit hides wires, stores the set-top box and router, and makes the whole room look finished. Here are ideas and practical rules.
**Floating (wall-mounted) unit:** a low cabinet fixed to the wall with space below. Looks light and makes cleaning easy.
**Full wall panelling:** a laminate, veneer or fluted panel behind the TV with a cabinet below. Gives a premium, hotel-like feel.
**TV unit with shelves:** open shelves or a glass cabinet on one or both sides for books and showpieces.
**Partition unit:** in open-plan homes, a TV unit can double as a divider between living and dining.

The centre of the TV screen should be roughly at **eye level when seated** — for most sofas that is about 40 to 45 inches from the floor. Mounting the TV too high is the most common mistake and strains the neck.
Plan wires and power before the work starts
Ask the electrician to put **power and HDMI/antenna points behind the TV** position, not at the floor level.
Run a **conduit pipe** from the TV to the cabinet below so wires stay hidden.
Keep **ventilation holes** in the cabinet for the set-top box and router.
Add a **plug point inside the cabinet** for devices.
Decide the TV size before panelling. The panel and cut-outs are planned around it.
Drawers for remote controls, chargers and documents.
A flap-down or open section for the set-top box (so the remote signal reaches it).
Closed cabinets for things you do not want on display.
Warm **profile lights** behind the panel or under the floating unit create a soft glow and reduce eye strain at night. Read our [lighting basics](/blog/home-lighting-guide/) for more.
See our [TV unit designs](/furniture/tv-units/) with estimated prices, or [ask for a custom design](/get-quote/).

title: Home lighting basics: warm, cool and profile lights
desc: A simple guide to home lighting: warm vs cool light, layering, profile and cove lights, and how much light each room needs.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Good lighting changes how a room feels more than almost anything else, and it costs little compared to furniture. Yet it is often planned last. Here are the basics we follow in our interior projects.
Light colour is measured in kelvin (K).
Many homes in India use only cool white tube lights. Mixing in warm light in living and bedrooms makes evenings much more relaxing.
**General (ambient) light:** ceiling lights or panel lights that light the whole room.
**Task light:** focused light where you work — under kitchen cabinets, above the study table, a reading lamp.
**Accent light:** profile lights in panelling, cove lights in a false ceiling, or a spotlight on art.
Put different layers on different switches. That way the same room can be bright for cleaning and soft for watching a film.
**Profile lights** are LED strips set in aluminium channels — in wardrobes, TV panelling, shelves and under kitchen cabinets.
**Cove lights** hide inside a false ceiling and wash the ceiling with soft light. See our [false ceiling cost guide](/guides/false-ceiling-cost-mumbai/).
**Living room:** a mix of ceiling lights, cove light and a lamp near the sofa.
**Bedroom:** warm light, bedside reading lights and a soft night light. Avoid a bright light directly above the pillow.
**Kitchen:** neutral white with under-cabinet lights so you are not working in your own shadow.
**Wardrobe:** sensor lights inside that switch on when the door opens.
**Bathroom:** good light at the mirror for shaving and make-up.
Use **LED** everywhere; it is efficient and lasts long.
Keep **drivers accessible** — the small transformers for LED strips fail more often than the strips and must be reachable.
Plan switch positions at the **bed and the door**, so you are not walking in the dark.
Planning a full interior? Our [home interiors](/services/home-interiors/) team designs lighting together with furniture so wiring is done once.

title: How to read an interior quotation (and spot hidden costs)
desc: What a good interior quotation should include, how per sq ft rates work, and the hidden costs to ask about before you sign.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Two interior quotations for the same flat can differ by lakhs — and often they are not quoting the same thing. Knowing how to read a quotation protects your budget and avoids arguments later.
**Room-wise items** — for example Bedroom 1: wardrobe, loft, bed, side tables.
**Size of each item** in feet and inches.
**How it is charged** — per square foot, per running foot, per piece or a fixed (lump sum) price.
**Material and grade** — plywood brand and grade, laminate or veneer, hardware type.
**What is included** — fitting, transport, handles, edge banding, polish.
**What is not included** — electrical, painting, civil work, GST.
Per square foot: how it is measured

Most furniture in Mumbai is priced per square foot of **front area** (width × height). A wardrobe 7 feet wide and 7 feet high is 49 sq ft. Lofts are usually priced separately. Kitchens are sometimes priced by **running foot** of counter. Always check how area is calculated, because "per sq ft" from two contractors may not measure the same way.
**Hardware upgrades** — soft-close hinges and channels may be "extra".
**Handles and profile lights** — often not included.
**Transport and lift charges**, especially in older buildings.
**Society deposits** for renovation (paid to the society, not the contractor).
**Electrical and painting work** linked to the furniture.
Ask every contractor for the same list of items with the same sizes and materials. Only then can you compare prices fairly.

On **contract basis**, the contractor supplies material and labour for one price. On **labour basis**, you buy the material and pay only for work. Each has pros and cons — read our [contract vs labour basis guide](/guides/contract-vs-labour-basis-interior/).
A common and fair pattern is an advance on signing, a payment when the framework is complete, and the balance on completion. Avoid paying the full amount before work starts.
Check that every item and size is listed.
Agree on the timeline and what happens if it slips.
Keep everything **in writing**, including changes made later.
We give clear, item-wise quotations after a free site visit. [Ask for an estimate](/get-quote/).

title: How long does a 2BHK interior take? A week-by-week timeline
desc: A realistic week-by-week timeline for 2BHK interior work in Mumbai — from design and society permission to furniture, painting and handover.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: "How many days will it take?" is one of the first questions every family asks. For a typical 2BHK with wardrobes, a kitchen, TV unit, beds and painting, the honest answer is usually **6 to 10 weeks**, depending on the scope and how quickly decisions are made. Here is how the time usually breaks down.
**Design and quotation** — layouts, materials and finishes.
**Society permission** — many housing societies need a written application and sometimes a deposit before renovation starts. See our [society rules guide](/blog/housing-society-renovation-rules/).
Delays before work starts are usually decision delays. Choose laminates and hardware early, and keep a shortlist ready.
Civil changes, if any; electrical points and conduits
False ceiling framing; plumbing changes for kitchen and bathrooms
Carpentry: wardrobe and kitchen carcasses, lofts, TV unit
Shutters, laminates, edge banding, hardware fitting
Painting and polishing; kitchen counter (granite or quartz)
Lights, final electrical fittings, cleaning and handover
Work in parallel shortens the timeline. For example, beds and tables can be made in the [workshop](/services/furniture-to-measure/) while carpentry continues on site.
Changing designs after carpentry has started.
Material shortages — specific laminate shades can take time to arrive.
Monsoon, when transport and drying times are slower.
Waiting for other contractors (electrician, plumber, painter) to finish.

On **contract basis**, the contractor coordinates materials and usually controls the timeline better. On **labour basis**, delays in material purchase by the owner can stop work. Read [contract vs labour basis](/guides/contract-vs-labour-basis-interior/) for the trade-offs.
Agree on the design fully before carpentry starts.
Approve material samples in one visit.
Keep payments as per the schedule so work does not pause.
Check progress weekly and note decisions in writing.
For a budget estimate alongside the timeline, see our [2BHK interior cost guide](/guides/2bhk-interior-cost-mumbai-thane/).

title: Renovating a flat in a Mumbai housing society: what to know
desc: Common housing society rules for flat renovation in Mumbai — permission letters, deposits, work timings, debris and neighbours — and how to plan for them.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Most flats in Mumbai, Thane and Navi Mumbai are in co-operative housing societies, and each society has its own rules for renovation. Knowing them early avoids stopped work and unhappy neighbours. Rules differ from society to society, so always check yours — here are the things most societies ask about.
A **list of contractors and workers**, sometimes with ID copies for security.
A **refundable deposit**, returned after checking common areas for damage.
Drawings, if you plan **structural or plumbing changes**.
Never break or alter load-bearing walls, columns or beams. Structural changes need proper approval and a structural engineer — and many are not allowed at all.
Societies usually allow noisy work only during fixed hours on weekdays, with restrictions on Sundays and holidays. Plan carpentry machine work and drilling within these hours.
Some societies ask that materials use the **service lift** only, or only at certain times.
Protect lift walls and floors with sheets while moving plywood and furniture.
Debris cannot be left in the compound. Ask your contractor whether **debris removal** is included in the quotation, and how often it will be cleared.
A short note to your neighbours before work starts, with the expected timeline and a phone number, prevents most complaints. Tell them about especially noisy days in advance.
Changes to bathroom floors can cause leaks into the flat below. If you are retiling a bathroom, do proper **waterproofing** and a water test before tiling, and inform the society if they require it.

We follow society rules on every project and help you prepare the work details your society asks for. See our [home interiors](/services/home-interiors/) service, or the [project timeline](/blog/2bhk-interior-timeline/).

title: Planning a small office interior: layout, storage and comfort
desc: How to plan a small office interior in Mumbai — workstation sizes, meeting space, storage, wiring and acoustics — without wasting expensive floor area.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Office space in Mumbai is expensive, so every square foot must earn its keep. A good small office fits the team comfortably, impresses visitors and is easy to change as the business grows.
Count how many people sit at desks every day, how many visit, and how often you meet. A team that is on the phone all day needs different space from a design studio that spreads out drawings.
Linear workstations in rows use space most efficiently. Add **low partitions** with a pin-up board for privacy without blocking light.
A **small meeting room** for 4–6 people is more useful than a large conference room used once a month.
**Glass partitions** keep cabins private but let daylight reach the whole office.
A **reception counter** with a branded wall creates a good first impression even in a small space.
**Mobile pedestals** (drawer units on wheels) under each desk.
**Full-height storage walls** along one side for files and supplies.
A lockable cabinet for documents and valuables.
Plan **power, LAN and charging points** at every desk before the furniture is made, with cable trays inside workstations. Retrofitting wires later is messy and costly.
Keep the server or router area ventilated and accessible — it should not be inside a closed cabinet with no air.
**Ergonomic chairs** matter more than expensive desks.
**Acoustic panels** or fabric pin boards reduce echo in rooms with hard floors and glass.
Neutral white light (around 4000K) is good for work areas.
Office fit-outs often have to be done at night or on weekends in commercial buildings. Agree on work hours with the building management in advance.
See our [office interiors](/services/office-interiors/) service, or [ask for a site visit](/get-quote/).

title: Shop and showroom fit-out tips that help you sell more
desc: Retail fit-out tips for shops and showrooms: the entrance zone, display heights, lighting, billing counter and storage that help customers buy.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: A shop's interior is part of its sales team. The right layout guides customers to products, the right lighting makes them look good, and smart storage keeps the floor tidy. Here is what we focus on in shop and showroom fit-outs.
The first few feet matter most
The area just inside the entrance is where customers slow down and look around. Keep it **open and uncluttered**, and place a striking display a few steps in — not right at the door.
Display and storage, not daily selling
Products at eye level sell best. Keep the most profitable items there.
Use **bright general light** so the shop feels open.
Add **spotlights or track lights** on key displays.
Choose light colour by product — warm light flatters wood and fabrics; neutral to cool light suits electronics and hardware.
Light the **shop front** well so it stands out in the evening.
Lights inside display cabinets and under shelves make products stand out and are inexpensive to add during the fit-out.

Place the counter where staff can see the entrance and the floor. Include drawers for cash and documents, space for a computer and printer, and a small display of add-on items customers can pick up while paying.
Shops always need more storage than expected. Build **storage under display units**, a back store with full-height shelving, and a lockable cabinet for valuable stock.
Retail furniture gets heavy daily use. Choose **thicker laminates**, strong hardware and metal-edged shelves where trolleys and boxes knock against them.
Mall fit-outs come with design approvals, fire safety requirements and fixed night-time work hours. We have experience working to mall guidelines — see [mall work](/services/mall-work/).
For standalone stores, see our [shops and showrooms](/services/shops-showrooms/) service.

title: How to clean and care for wooden furniture
desc: Simple, safe ways to clean and maintain solid wood, veneer and laminate furniture so it looks good for years — what to use and what to avoid.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Good furniture can last decades if it is looked after. Most care is simple and takes only a few minutes a week. The right method depends on the finish, so start by knowing what your furniture is made of.
**Dust regularly** with a soft, dry microfibre cloth. Dust is abrasive and dulls the finish over time.
**Wipe spills immediately** with a damp, well-wrung cloth, then dry the area.
Use a cloth slightly damp with water and a drop of mild soap for marks. Dry immediately.
Avoid harsh cleaners, ammonia and alcohol, which can damage polish.
Re-polish when the surface looks dull or patchy — usually every few years, depending on use.
Keep furniture **out of strong direct sunlight**, which fades and dries wood.

Laminate is the easiest to care for. Wipe with a damp cloth and mild detergent. For stubborn marks, a soft cloth with a little diluted cleaner is fine. Avoid scrubbing pads, which leave scratches on glossy laminate.
Use only a **soft microfibre cloth** and water or a cleaner made for acrylic. Paper towels and rough cloths cause fine scratches that show on gloss.
Test any new cleaner on a hidden spot first, such as the inside of a door.
Tighten handle screws when they loosen, keep **sliding wardrobe tracks** free of dust, and adjust hinges if doors stop aligning. A little attention prevents bigger repairs.
Look out for small holes, fine powder below furniture, or mud lines on walls. Act quickly — read our [termite protection guide](/blog/termite-protection-furniture/).
For the monsoon season specifically, see [monsoon care for wooden furniture](/blog/monsoon-care-wooden-furniture-mumbai/).

title: Termite protection for furniture: prevention and early signs
desc: How termites damage furniture in Mumbai homes, the early warning signs, and practical prevention for new and existing wooden furniture.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Termites are a common problem in humid cities like Mumbai. They eat wood from the inside, so damage often goes unnoticed until a shutter crumbles or a skirting breaks. Prevention is much cheaper than replacing furniture.
**Mud tubes or lines** on walls, especially near skirting and wardrobe sides.
**Fine powder or tiny pellets** below furniture.
**Small holes** on surfaces, or paint and laminate bubbling.
Swarms of winged insects near lights, often after the first rains.
If you see mud tubes, do not just scrape them off. Termites are coming from somewhere — call professional pest control to treat the source.
Ask for **treated plywood** or boards with anti-termite treatment.
Apply **anti-termite chemical treatment** to walls and floors before built-in furniture is fixed, especially in ground floor flats.
Use **solid wood that is properly seasoned and treated**. Teak's natural oils help it resist termites better than many woods.
Keep a small **gap between furniture and damp walls**.
Get **periodic pest control** from a licensed provider, as many families do once a year.
Fix **leaks and dampness** quickly — termites love moisture.
Do not store cardboard boxes and old newspapers on the floor or in lofts for long.
Check lofts, the back of wardrobes and under beds a few times a year.
What to do if you find termites
Do not disturb the area too much; note where you see them
Call a professional pest control service
Remove badly damaged pieces after treatment
Repair or replace damaged boards with treated material

No material is completely immune, but plywood and boards made with proper treatment, **BWP grade** in damp areas, and metal or PVC in very damp spots reduce the risk. Our [plywood, MDF and solid wood guide](/guides/plywood-mdf-solid-wood-furniture/) explains the grades.
For general care, see [how to clean and care for wooden furniture](/blog/caring-for-wooden-furniture/).

title: Pooja unit (mandir) design ideas for apartments
desc: Pooja unit and home mandir ideas for small apartments — wall-mounted, corner and cabinet mandirs, materials, lighting and practical tips.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: A pooja unit is often the most personal piece of furniture in an Indian home. In compact Mumbai flats, a separate pooja room is rare, so the mandir has to fit beautifully into a living room, dining area or corner. Here are ideas that work.
**Wall-mounted mandir:** a floating unit with a shelf for idols and a drawer below for diyas and agarbatti. Saves floor space.
**Corner mandir:** uses an unused corner, often with shelves on two sides.
**Cabinet mandir with doors:** closes when not in use — useful in a living room or when the mandir is near the dining table.
**Floor-standing unit:** a larger mandir with storage below for pooja items and books.
Keep the **diya area heat-safe** — use a metal or stone base where lamps are lit, not laminate.
Plan a **drawer or small cabinet** for matchboxes, incense, books and cloth.
Leave **ventilation** for smoke from agarbatti and diyas.
Add a **warm LED light** inside, on its own switch.
Consider a **bell hook** and a small shelf for flowers.
Many families follow traditional guidance on direction and placement. Tell your designer what matters to your family so the unit is planned around it.

For a wall-mounted mandir, a width of about 2 to 3 feet and a depth of 12 to 15 inches suits most homes. Keep the idol shelf at a height that is comfortable when standing or sitting, depending on how your family prays.

Every home and tradition is different, so mandirs are usually made to measure. We make pooja units in solid wood and engineered wood with jali work and lighting — see [furniture to measure](/services/furniture-to-measure/) or [send us a photo](/get-quote/) of the space.

title: Kids' room furniture: safe, smart and grows with your child
desc: How to plan safe, practical furniture for a child's room — rounded corners, anchored wardrobes, study tables, storage and designs that grow with age.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Children's rooms need furniture that is safe today and still useful in five or ten years. Bright themes are fun, but a few basic choices matter much more.
**Rounded corners and edges** on tables, beds and shelves.
**Anchor tall furniture to the wall** — wardrobes, bookshelves and dressers can tip if a child climbs them.
**Soft-close hinges and drawers** to protect small fingers.
**No glass** in low cabinets; use acrylic or laminate instead.
**Child-safe locks** on cabinets with medicines or tools.
Keep **electrical points** behind furniture or use covers.
A loft or upper bunk needs a strong guard rail on all open sides and a sturdy ladder. Bunk beds are generally not recommended for very young children.
Low open shelves, toy storage bins, a small table and chair
Study table with drawers, bookshelf, pin-up board
Full-size study desk, larger wardrobe, space for a computer
Choose a **wardrobe with adjustable shelves** and a **bed size** that will still fit a teenager — a single bed of 3 × 6.5 feet lasts much longer than a toddler bed.
A desk about **2 to 2.5 feet deep** gives enough room for books and a laptop.
**Good light** from the left for right-handed children (and the right for left-handed ones), plus a desk lamp.
An adjustable chair so feet rest flat on the floor.
A **pin-up board** or magnetic board for timetables and artwork.
Children tidy up more when storage is easy: open bins at their height, labelled drawers, and hooks for school bags. Keep rarely used items in the loft.

**Matt laminate** in light or pastel shades hides fingerprints and survives crayons better than gloss. Add colour through bedding, wall paint or removable decals, which are easy to change as tastes change.
See our [study tables](/furniture/study/) and [beds](/furniture/beds/), or ask us to design a full kids' room.

title: Balcony makeover ideas for Mumbai flats
desc: Turn a small Mumbai balcony into a sitting nook, garden or work corner — weather-proof furniture, flooring, privacy and monsoon tips.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Even a small balcony can become the favourite spot in a Mumbai flat — a place for morning tea, plants or a quiet work corner. The key is choosing materials that survive sun, salty air and heavy rain.
Decide how you will use it
**Sitting nook:** two chairs and a small table, or a built-in bench with storage inside.
**Garden:** railing planters, a vertical garden on one wall and a small stool.
**Work corner:** a fold-down wall desk if the balcony is covered and dry.
**Utility:** a washing machine cabinet and drying rack, neatly enclosed.
Yes, if the coating is good
Only in a fully covered, dry balcony
In the monsoon, move cushions inside or use quick-drying outdoor fabric. Fold-up furniture is easy to store when the rain blows in.
Wooden-look **deck tiles** that click together are a quick upgrade and can be lifted for cleaning. Make sure water can still drain to the outlet.
Bamboo or outdoor roller **blinds** cut glare and give privacy from neighbours.
**Trellis panels** with climbers create a green screen.
Check society rules before installing permanent grills or enclosures — see our [society renovation guide](/blog/housing-society-renovation-rules/).
Warm string lights or a waterproof wall light make the balcony usable in the evening. Use outdoor-rated fittings and a covered plug point.
Use the **walls** — planters and shelves keep the floor free.
Stick to **two or three colours** so it looks calm, not cluttered.
Want a built-in bench, planter boxes or a utility cabinet made to size? See [furniture to measure](/services/furniture-to-measure/).

title: Wall finishes compared: paint, texture, wallpaper and panelling
desc: Emulsion paint, texture, wallpaper and wall panelling compared for Indian homes — looks, cost, durability in humidity and where each works best.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: Walls are the largest surface in any room, so the finish sets the mood. Here is a simple comparison of the four main options for homes in Mumbai.
The most common finish. Modern emulsions come in matt, satin and sheen finishes.
**Washable** emulsions are worth it in kitchens, kids' rooms and corridors.
In humid areas, choose an **anti-fungal** paint and fix dampness first.
Texture creates patterns — sand, stucco, rustic or designer effects — on one feature wall.
Best used on **one wall** behind a bed or sofa; too much texture feels busy.
Modern wallpapers include vinyl and non-woven types with thousands of designs.
Quick to install and makes a big visual change.
Choose **vinyl wallpaper** in humid rooms; avoid paper wallpaper near bathrooms and kitchens.
Must go on a **dry, smooth wall** — dampness causes peeling.
Panels in laminate, veneer, fluted MDF or PVC give a premium, hotel-like look.
Great behind beds and TV units — see our [TV unit ideas](/blog/tv-unit-design-ideas/).
Costs more than paint but lasts long and needs little upkeep.
Fix seepage and dampness before any finish. Every option — even expensive panelling — will fail on a wet wall.
Light, warm neutrals make small rooms feel larger. Use deeper colours on one wall, and repeat a colour from your furniture or curtains so the room feels connected.
Planning walls together with furniture gives the best result. See our [home interiors](/services/home-interiors/) service.

title: Choosing a dining table: size, shape and seating
desc: How to choose the right dining table size and shape for your home — seating space per person, clearance, 4, 6 and 8 seater sizes and materials.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: A dining table is where families eat, children do homework and guests gather. Picking the right size and shape makes the dining area comfortable instead of cramped.
Each person needs roughly **2 feet (24 inches) of table width** to eat comfortably. A table depth of about **3 feet** leaves room for serving dishes in the middle.
Keep at least **2.5 to 3 feet** between the table edge and the wall or other furniture, so people can pull out chairs and walk behind seated guests.
Measure your dining space and subtract about 6 feet from each side for chairs and walking room. What is left is the largest table that will fit comfortably.
**Rectangular:** the most common; fits long, narrow dining areas.
**Round:** friendly for conversation and good in square spaces; no sharp corners for children.
**Square:** good for 4 people in compact homes.
**Extendable or folding:** ideal for small flats that host family on weekends.
A **bench** on one side seats more people in less space and slides under the table. Chairs with arms are comfortable but need more width.
Standard dining height is about **29 to 30 inches**, with chair seats around 17 to 18 inches. If you plan a counter-height table, use bar stools instead.
See our [dining sets](/furniture/dining/) with estimated prices, or order a table made to your exact size.

title: Upgrading a rented flat: changes you can take with you
desc: Ideas to make a rented flat in Mumbai feel like home without major renovation — freestanding furniture, lighting, curtains and storage you can take along.
author: Mumbai Interior team
body: In Mumbai, many families live in rented flats for years. You may not want to spend on built-in work you will leave behind, but you still want a home that feels like yours. The answer is to invest in things that move with you.
A **freestanding wardrobe** instead of a fitted one.
A **TV console** on legs instead of wall panelling.
**Bookshelves and sideboards** that can go into your next home.
Furniture made to measure can still be freestanding — built to fit typical Mumbai room sizes so it works in the next flat too.
Before ordering, think about your next likely flat. Modular pieces that can be rearranged are more flexible than one large unit.
**Curtains and blinds** — full-height curtains make ceilings look higher.
**Lighting** — floor lamps, table lamps and plug-in wall lights add warmth without wiring. See our [lighting basics](/blog/home-lighting-guide/).
**Rugs** — define the living area and hide worn flooring.
**Plants** — easy to move and they make any room feel fresh.
**Cushions and throws** — change colours seasonally at low cost.
Some changes — a new coat of paint, a few hooks, or a kitchen chimney — may be acceptable to the landlord, especially if they add value. Get agreement **in writing** before drilling or painting.

If you expect to stay three years or more, a few built-in pieces can still make sense — especially kitchen storage and a wardrobe. Discuss with the landlord whether they will share the cost, since the improvement stays with the flat.
Browse our [furniture](/furniture/) — every piece is made to order and built to move with you.
